title: Abigail (1 Samuel 25)
hookLine: a wise woman rides out with bread and figs and talks David out of revenge
last: I WILL NOT LIFT MY HAND.

lines: ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED MEN SET OUT.
cards: David spared a king in a cave. Here he nearly kills a farmer over a rude reply. The farmer is Nabal, a rich man with three thousand sheep, shearing them in Carmel.
David's men have kept Nabal's shepherds safe out in the fields, and now David sends ten young men to ask, politely, for whatever Nabal can spare for a feast day. Nabal sneers. Who is David?
There are plenty of runaway servants these days. Why should I give my bread to men I don't know? David gives one order: every man, gird on your sword.
About four hundred of them set out.

teach.b: One of Nabal's servants runs to his wife, Abigail. The text calls her a woman of good understanding, and her husband churlish and evil in his doings.

teach.h: SHE LOADS THE DONKEYS AND RIDES.
teach.b: She loads donkeys: two hundred loaves, two bottles of wine, five sheep ready dressed, parched corn, a hundred clusters of raisins and two hundred cakes of figs.

She sends them ahead, rides after them, and tells Nabal nothing. On a hillside path she meets David coming down with his army. She gets off her donkey, bows to the ground, and takes the blame on herself.
Her husband, she says, is just like his name: "as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him."
Then the thing David needs to hear: when you are king one day, don't let this be a stumbling block on your conscience, that you shed blood without cause and avenged yourself with your own hand.
She isn't only saving her household.

And he hears it, in the King James Bible: "Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, which sent thee this day to meet me: And blessed be thy advice, and blessed be thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself with mine own hand."
He blesses God for sending her, her advice, and her. In the cave, David held himself back. Here someone else had to, and he was humble enough to let her.
Later in the chapter Nabal dies, and David asks Abigail to be his wife.

how: Some Christians tell Abigail's story as an example of courageous peacemaking and wise speech, and it is read in Bible studies about anger, conflict and the gift of a wise friend.

games.q: you're Abigail. your husband has insulted David, and about four hundred armed men are on their way. what do you do?
o: load bread, wine and figs, and ride out to meet him.
games.why: she loads the donkeys, rides out without telling Nabal, bows to the ground and talks David out of revenge. he blesses her advice.

practice: Picture someone near you riding down the hill with their sword on, like a friend about to send an angry message.
Think the way Abigail did, not how to win the argument but what would help them see their better self: bread first, words second. If you pray, ask for her kind of wisdom in your own words.
